payload.title: get_for_provider_account picks rows[0] arbitrarily on duplicates
payload.body: no unique index on (user_id,auth_provider,provider_user_id) on legacy tables; sort deterministically or add partial unique index

payload.reason: Fixed: get_for_provider_account (and get_by_provider) now rank rows newest-first via the shared _newest_first helper — refreshed_at, then created_at, tie-broken on identity_id — instead of returning rows[0] in driver order. Covered by 4 tests in tests/unit/identity/test_identity_store.py::TestDuplicateRowOrdering.

Fixed: get_live_provider_token now refreshes under a per-(user, external account) asyncio guard (ExternalAuth._refresh_guard) and re-reads the credential inside it, so a concurrent loser returns the winner's rotation instead of spending a retired refresh token. Guard entries are dropped once nobody holds or awaits them. In-process only — documented in the method's Note; the re-read, not the lock, is what keeps a second worker safe. Covered by tests/unit/identity/test_external_token_capture.py::TestConcurrentRefresh (3 tests; the double-refresh test fails with the guard removed).

Fixed: IdentityStore.update_tokens now re-seals id_token (only when the refresh returned one, so an omitting provider does not erase the stored copy) and get_live_provider_token republishes session["id_token"] after a rotation, so the published OIDC token no longer outlives its own exp. Covered by tests/unit/identity/test_identity_store.py::TestUpdateTokens and tests/unit/identity/test_external_token_capture.py::TestRefreshedIdToken (4 tests, including the omit-case guard rails).

Fixed: ExternalAuth._vault_upstream_token now returns bool (True only after save_linked_identity succeeds) and capture_login_credential sets CAPTURED_LOGIN_GRANT only on that True, so an unbound grant or a failed vault write leaves the AS-resume legacy re-save available. Covered by tests/unit/identity/test_external_token_capture.py::TestCaptureMarker (2 tests) plus the existing suppression control test.

payload.title: A failing migration in ensure_identity_columns silently blocks every later one
payload.body:
navigator_auth/identity/migrations.py:ensure_identity_columns runs _MIGRATION_FILES in one `for` loop with no per-file error handling, and setup_identity_columns wraps the whole loop in a single try/except that only logs. So the first file that raises stops every later file from running, and startup continues as if the schema were fine.

This is reachable, not theoretical: 001_identity_credentials.sql ends with `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_user_identities_provider_account ON auth.user_identities (user_id, auth_provider, provider_user_id) WHERE provider_user_id IS NOT NULL`. `IF NOT EXISTS` does not help when the index does not exist but the table already holds duplicate rows for that key — Postgres raises on creation. A legacy database with duplicates therefore never gets 002-005 (id_token column, key_version type, the base columns UserIdentity requires, the legacy uid default), and the only symptom is one WARNING line.

Related: issue:c9c05c53ec05 made IdentityStore.get_for_provider_account resolve duplicates deterministically in Python precisely because that index cannot be relied upon.

Suggested fix is a design call, not a one-liner — whoever takes it must decide whether later migrations may run after an earlier one failed. Options: run each file in its own try/except and report a per-file result; or keep the fail-fast loop but make the failure loud (raise at startup, or a health-check flag) instead of a warning; and/or de-duplicate before creating the index (or create it CONCURRENTLY/validate separately) so 001 cannot wedge the chain.

payload.title: Entra reuses its cached access token on re-login, so the new session gets a stale provider token
payload.body:
**What is wrong.** Logging out of Navigator and logging back in through `AzureAuth` does not yield a fresh provider access token. `AuthHandler.logout` / `UserSession.logout` call `session.invalidate()`, which ends only the *Navigator* session; the Entra SSO/KMSI session survives. The next authorization-code round-trip is therefore silent at the IdP, and Entra's token endpoint returns its own **cached** access token — same `iat`, same `exp` — with `expires_in` set to the token's *remaining* lifetime rather than its issued lifetime. `ExternalAuth.build_user_info` (`navigator_auth/backends/external.py:993,1003`) then publishes that already-aged token into the brand-new session, and `capture_login_credential` vaults it.

**Measured on 2026-10-23 (real Entra login, tenant af176793-…, appid bbc8ff0c-… navigator-auth):**

- access token: `iat` 2026-10-22T23:56:59Z, `exp` 2026-10-23T01:27:56Z → issued lifetime `exp - iat` = 5457 s
- vault row (`auth.user_identities`): `refreshed_at` 2026-10-23T00:02:00.495Z, `expires_at` 2026-10-23T01:27:55.538Z → 5155.04 s
- `5457 - 5155 = 302 s`; the gap from `iat` to the vault write is `301 s`; the vault `expires_at` matches the token `exp` to within 0.5 s

So a second round-trip 5 minutes later stored **the same token**, and `expires_in` reported only what was left of it.

**Why it matters.**
1. A consumer reading `session["auth_token"]` directly gets a credential that may be nearly expired at the moment of login. `get_live_provider_token` (G4) refreshes on demand and so is unaffected, but the session copy is only rewritten on refresh (`external.py:847`) — the login path never re-publishes a fresher one.
2. It silently invalidates any experiment that measures token lifetime across logins, including FEAT-103 §8 Q1: a reading can describe a token issued by an earlier process with different settings. The first Q1 attempt failed exactly this way.
3. It means `expires_in` from the provider is not the issued lifetime. Convention B1 (`expires_in` is seconds) is still satisfied, but nothing should infer a *lifetime* from it.

**Suggested fix.** Treat provider-token freshness as explicit rather than assumed. Options, cheapest first: (a) record the token's `iat` alongside `external_expires_at` so staleness is observable; (b) on the login path, run the capture through the same leeway check `get_live_provider_token` uses, and refresh before publishing when the captured grant is already inside `IDENTITY_REFRESH_LEEWAY`; (c) where a genuinely fresh credential is required, send `prompt=login` on the authorization request so Entra re-issues instead of serving its cache. (c) changes login UX and should not be the default.

payload.title: AzureAuth user/password path: acquire_token_silent cache hit skips the entire login body
payload.body:
**What is wrong.** In `AzureAuth.authenticate` (`navigator_auth/backends/azure.py`), the username/password branch first tries the MSAL cache:

```python
accounts = app.get_accounts(username=user)
result = None
if accounts:
    result = app.acquire_token_silent(Default_SCOPE, account=accounts[0])   # azure.py:168
if not result:                                                              # azure.py:169
    result = app.acquire_token_by_username_password(user, pwd, Default_SCOPE)
    ...
    grant = self._token_from_msal_result(...)
    userdata, uid = self.build_user_info(...)
    data = await self.validate_user_info(...)
    await self.capture_login_credential(request, grant)
    return self.home_redirect(...)
```

Everything that constitutes the login — `_token_from_msal_result`, the userinfo call, `build_user_info`, `validate_user_info`, `capture_login_credential` and the redirect — lives **inside** `if not result:`. When `acquire_token_silent` succeeds, `result` is truthy, the whole block is skipped, and the function falls through with the token discarded: no session, no capture, no redirect.

**Why it matters.** On a cache hit the user is not logged in at all, and the branch returns whatever follows instead of a session. In practice the hit is rare — `get_msal_client` is handed a freshly constructed `msal.SerializableTokenCache()` on every request (`azure.py:162-163`), so the cache is almost always empty and the silent call almost always returns `None`, which is why this has gone unnoticed. Any change that makes the cache persist across requests would turn it into a hard login failure.

**Pre-existing**, not introduced by FEAT-103: Module 3 added `capture_login_credential` *inside* the existing `if not result:` block and did not change the control flow. Recorded here so the two are not conflated. The browser authorization-code path (`auth_callback`, `azure.py:267-271`) is unaffected.

**Suggested fix.** Hoist the post-token work out of the `if not result:` block so both the silent-hit and the password paths fall through into one shared "we have a result" body, and raise/redirect explicitly when `result` carries no `access_token`. Covering it needs a test with a pre-seeded token cache, which no current test does.

payload.title: Dev DB auth.user_identities has legacy 'uid' column; UserIdentity.filter() fails on it
payload.body: After FEAT-104 TASK-114 (nullable token columns) the UserIdentity insert succeeds on the dev DB, but hydration (filter/get) raises 'unexpected keyword argument uid' because the physical table keeps a legacy uid column. 3 tests in tests/test_token_exchange_backend.py (test_linked_identity_precedence, test_vaults_credential_not_session, test_reexchange_preserves_refresh_token) newly fail against that DB (they passed before only because the insert failed early and was swallowed). Fix: migrate/drop the legacy uid column in the dev DB or have the tests honour vault_schema_ok.

payload.reason: Fixed on feat-FEAT-103-external-provider-token-capture. Options (a) + (b) of the suggested fix, with (c) as an opt-in: (b) ExternalAuth.ensure_fresh_login_grant runs the captured grant through the same IDENTITY_REFRESH_LEEWAY check get_live_provider_token uses and refreshes before the grant reaches the provider userinfo call, the session or the vault; it never fails a login (a declined/raising refresh keeps the provider's credential, with a warning) and the rotation inherits the login's provider_user_id / id_token / scopes when it omits them. AzureAuth wires both login paths (auth_callback and the username/password branch). (a) TokenResponse gains issued_at — the access token's own iat, read unverified via jwt_issued_at and documented as observability only — plus age_seconds(); build_user_info publishes external_issued_at beside external_expires_at, and get_live_provider_token republishes it after a rotation, so a provider-cached token is visible without decoding anything. (c) New AZURE_LOGIN_PROMPT setting (empty by default, so login UX is unchanged) sends the OIDC prompt on the authorization request; `login` makes Entra re-authenticate and issue instead of replaying its cache — this is the supported lever for point 2 of the revised spec §8 Q1 protocol, and §8 Q1 plus §7 Known Risks, docs/vault.rst, docs/settings.rst, the /api/v1/demo/token-claims instrument and CHANGELOG.md were updated accordingly. Covered by 15 new tests: TestStaleLoginGrant (8) in tests/unit/identity/test_external_token_capture.py, TestIssuedAt (5) in tests/unit/identity/test_token_response.py, TestAuthCallbackFreshness (2) in tests/test_azure_token_verifier.py. Full suite: 37 failed / 1589 passed / 4 skipped, FAILED node-id set identical to the recorded FEAT-103 baseline (zero new failures). Independent codex review of the uncommitted diff raised no findings. NOT fixed by this (unchanged by design): the Navigator JWT minted by validate_user_info still carries the pre-refresh external_expires_at in its extra claims, since the login-path refresh happens after the grant is captured but the session — the system of record — is corrected; and nothing forces a fresh issue when AZURE_LOGIN_PROMPT is empty.

Login body dedented out of the `if not result:` cache-miss branch in AzureAuth.authenticate(); a silent-token cache hit now runs the same profile fetch / validate / capture / home_redirect path as the username-password grant. Covered by tests/test_azure_userpass_login.py (3 tests; the cache-hit one fails on the pre-fix code).

ensure_identity_columns now runs each migration file in its own try/except: a failure is logged with the offending filename, the remaining files still run (each guards its own effect on a catalog lookup, so none depends on a previous success), and the set is re-raised afterwards as one RuntimeError naming every failed file, chained to the first exception. setup_identity_columns still never raises, but now logs that summary instead of only the first error. Regression tests in tests/unit/identity/test_identity_migrations.py: a failing 003 no longer prevents 004/005/006 (all six attempted, error names 003 only), and the all-failing case reports 6 of 6. 179 identity unit tests pass; ruff clean.

Migration 006_identity_drop_legacy_uid.sql promotes identity_id to primary key (reusing 004's unique index) and drops the legacy uid column; registered in _MIGRATION_FILES after 005 (commits 64d18bd, 95d98e0). Verified against PostgreSQL 17.3 in three table shapes (legacy: drops, PK moves, rows preserved; canonical: no-op; legacy with a view on uid: warns and changes nothing, never CASCADE), each idempotent across a second run. On the dev `navigator` database uid is gone, identity_id is the PK, and UserIdentity.all() / .filter(user_id=...) both hydrate. 205 identity + token-exchange tests pass.

payload.title: Local ModelHandler calls json_response(content=...) which navigator-api 4.0.1 rejects; partner-key put/patch/post/delete fail (406/500)
payload.body: navigator_auth/handlers/model.py calls self.json_response(content=...) in get(:meta), put, patch, post, delete, _post_get; installed navigator BaseHandler.json_response takes 'response'. put/post insert get caught as 406 AFTER the row is inserted, so the return-once partner token is never delivered; patch/delete 500. Also delete() maps not-found to status 204 which error() turns into 400, and _post_get's fields branch reads the wrong variable. Fix: pass the payload positionally. FEAT-105 worked around _post_get only (partners.py).

payload.title: FEAT-105 _filtering returns full rows instead of upstream single-column autocomplete shape; has_*_token always false on that path
payload.body: Upstream ?_filter= returns only the filtered column's values; the override returns full allowlisted rows through _model_response (route behaviour change), and since safe_filter selects only public columns, has_refresh_token/has_id_token are always false there (drift vs IdentityStore.masked). Consider restoring single-column shape restricted to public_columns.

payload.title: ModelHandler.patch() not-found branches call no_content() without returning, so PATCH on a missing row 500s
payload.body: navigator_auth/handlers/model.py, ModelHandler.patch(): both not-found paths call `self.no_content(headers=headers)` and fall through. `no_content()` RETURNS a response (unlike `error()`/`critical()`, which raise), so execution continues: on NoDataFound `result` is unbound (UnboundLocalError), and on a falsy `result` the next line calls `result.get_fields()` on None (AttributeError). Either way PATCH of a missing row answers 500 instead of 204. Same shape as issue:7164a1f421ce (closed) but a separate defect, present on both dev and feat-FEAT-105. Fix: `return self.no_content(headers=headers)` in both branches.

payload.title: ModelHandler.post() empty-PK TypeError branch passes exception=<dict> to error(), losing the error body
payload.body: navigator_auth/handlers/model.py, ModelHandler.post(), the `else:` (no PK) branch: `return self.error(exception=error, status=406)` where `error` is the `{"error": ..., "payload": ...}` dict every other handler passes as `reason=`. `BaseHandler.error()` renders `exception` as `response_obj["reason"] = str(exception)` and then, because `response` is None, sets `body=None` — so the rendered dict is dropped and the 406 has an empty body. Every sibling branch in the same method uses `reason=error`. Fix: `return self.error(reason=error, status=406)`. Present on both dev and feat-FEAT-105.

payload.reason: Fixed on dev (merge 42b2060): both not-found branches of ModelHandler.patch() now return self.no_content(headers=headers), so a PATCH against a missing row answers 204 with the x-error header instead of 500 (UnboundLocalError after NoDataFound, AttributeError on None.get_fields()). Regression tests in tests/unit/test_model_handler_responses.py: test_patch_missing_row_is_no_content, test_patch_no_data_found_is_no_content, plus an AST guard (test_no_response_helper_result_is_discarded) that fails on any discarded no_content()/json_response()/response() call anywhere in the module. 467 unit tests pass; full suite matches the dev baseline. Still present on feat-FEAT-105 — that branch needs the same two-word change when it merges.

Fixed on dev (merge a55a45c): ModelHandler.post()'s no-PK TypeError/AttributeError/ValueError branch now passes reason=error instead of exception=error, so the 406 carries the error dict instead of a bare '406: Not Acceptable'. Measured against installed navigator 4.0.1: exception=<dict> -> body b'406: Not Acceptable'; reason=<dict> -> body b"406: {'error': ...}"; response=<dict> -> body b'{"error": ...}'. reason= matches all ten sibling branches, so that is what shipped. Regression tests in tests/unit/test_model_handler_responses.py: test_post_invalid_payload_reports_the_error plus an AST guard (test_every_error_call_names_its_payload) requiring every error() call in the module to pass reason= or response=. 469 unit tests pass; full suite matches the dev baseline. Follow-up filed: reason=<dict> renders a Python repr, not the JSON the content_type promises.

payload.title: ModelHandler error() calls pass dicts as reason=, producing a Python repr body and a dict HTTP reason phrase instead of JSON
payload.body:
All ~11 `self.error(reason=<dict>, status=...)` calls in navigator_auth/handlers/model.py rely on `reason` falling through `BaseHandler.error()`'s `**kwargs` into the aiohttp exception constructor. Measured against the installed navigator 4.0.1:

    self.error(reason={"error": "...", "payload": "..."}, status=406)
      -> reason  = {'error': '...', 'payload': '...'}   (the HTTP reason phrase is a dict)
      -> body    = b"406: {'error': '...', 'payload': '...'}"
      -> content_type = application/json

So the response advertises JSON but carries aiohttp's default `"<status>: <reason>"` text with a Python dict repr in it, and the dict also lands in the status line. `self.error(response=<dict>, status=...)` is the parameter that renders a real JSON body (`b'{"error": "...", "payload": "..."}'`) and leaves the reason phrase alone.

Not urgent and not a crash — clients have lived with it — but any consumer doing `await resp.json()` on a 4xx from ModelHandler fails to parse. Fix: switch the dict-carrying calls from `reason=` to `response=` across the module (and keep `reason=` for the string ones). This changes the wire format of every error response the handler emits, so it needs a deliberate call rather than a drive-by edit; tests/unit/test_model_handler_responses.py::test_every_error_call_names_its_payload already accepts either keyword. Same pattern exists on feat-FEAT-105.

payload.reason: Fixed on dev (merge c689fc2): the 16 dict-carrying error() calls in navigator_auth/handlers/model.py now pass response= instead of reason=, so every 4xx this handler emits is real JSON ({"error": ..., "payload": ...}) with the default reason phrase, matching its application/json content type. The f-string/str calls keep reason= — error() assigns a non-dict response to body and aiohttp rejects a str body. critical(reason=<dict>) was left alone: it declares reason and json.dumps it into {"message": ...}, so it already emitted valid JSON. Regression tests in tests/unit/test_model_handler_responses.py: test_error_body_is_json (parses a 400 body and asserts reason == 'Bad Request'), a strengthened test_post_invalid_payload_reports_the_error, and an AST guard test_structured_error_payloads_go_through_response that fails on any error(reason=<Name|Dict>) in the module. 471 unit tests pass; full suite FAILED node-id set identical to the recorded dev baseline, so no consumer of these bodies regressed. Same pattern still present on feat-FEAT-105.

payload.body: self.error(403) raised inside a try block is swallowed by except Exception and re-reported as 500. Pre-existing; pinned as-is by tests/test_auth_crud_write_envelope.py (TASK-157) and out of FEAT-107 scope. Fix: re-raise HTTP exceptions before the generic handler.

payload.title: UserRoleHandler.post: missing actor row gives 500; check-then-update not atomic
payload.body: If the actor row is missing, actor.get('is_staff') raises AttributeError (500, still fail-closed) - should be an explicit 403 with audit. The actor/target SELECT and the UPDATE are not in one transaction or FOR UPDATE, leaving a small TOCTOU window on the actor-holds-flag check. Also the request property/setter override on the class is a test-only accommodation in production code.

payload.title: UserManager: owner can DELETE their own account (confirm intent)
payload.body: authorize_row with payload=None allows the owner on user:delete, so a user can delete their own row via DELETE /api/v1/users/{id}. Spec does not forbid it; confirm intended, otherwise restrict delete to the admin path. Also: PATCH composite-pk path in navigator ModelView swallows the first HTTPForbidden in try/except print(ex) and relies on a second _set_update to refuse again - fragile, worth a pinning test.
